title: Satellite Image (True Colour)
sub: Sentinel-2 natural colour, post-monsoon (15 Oct - 30 Nov 2025) median
about: What the land looks like from space after the monsoon: green is active vegetation, brown and grey are open soil and rock, dark patches are water or dense shade.
data: Sentinel-2 L2A, 10 m, Cloud Score+ masked.
used: Context and visual check of all other layers.

title: Tree Canopy Cover
sub: Share of each 30 m cell under tree crowns >= 5 m tall
about: Canopy cover from a 1 m global canopy-height map: the share of each 30 m cell covered by trees at least 5 m tall. 40 % or more is dense forest (C1, protected).
data: Meta / WRI Global Canopy Height 1 m (read at 4.8 m); Hansen loss 2019+ removed.
used: N1 Canopy deficit; constraint C1; ANR and blank-area rules.

title: Canopy Height
about: Height of the vegetation canopy above the ground from a global 1 m model. Most of the range is below 2 m: open scrub and grass.
data: Meta / WRI Global Canopy Height 1 m (v1).
used: Source of canopy cover (A1) and dense-forest distance (F4).

title: Greenness at Peak Season (NDVI)
sub: Sentinel-2 NDVI, mid-October to November median 2021-2025
about: NDVI (Normalised Difference Vegetation Index) measures green leaf density: about 0.1 for bare soil, 0.3-0.5 for grass and scrub, above 0.6 for dense green vegetation.
data: Sentinel-2 L2A, 10 m, Cloud Score+ masked, 2021-2025.
used: N2 Bare soil at peak greenness (via vegetation cover).

title: Greenness in Dry Season (NDVI)
about: Green cover at the end of the dry season. Areas green in April-May hold evergreen trees, irrigated land or invasive evergreen shrubs.
data: Sentinel-2 L2A, 10 m, Cloud Score+ masked, 2021-2025.

title: Above-Ground Biomass
about: Above-ground woody biomass in tonnes of dry matter per hectare.
data: ESA CCI Above-Ground Biomass v6.0, 100 m.

title: Land Cover
about: Global 10 m land-cover map. It defines the natural-vegetation landscape used to scale the indicators and the built-up and cropland constraints.
used: Anchors (classes 10/20/30/60); C5 built-up; C6 cropland; C7 bare rock; G5.

title: Evergreen Shrub Invasion Signal
sub: Dry-season green, low seasonal change, canopy < 20 %
about: Pixels that stay green in April-May (NDVI 0.30-0.60), change little between seasons and have little tree canopy: the typical signature of invasive evergreen shrubs such as Prosopis juliflora or Lantana.
data: Sentinel-2 L2A, 10 m, Cloud Score+ masked, 2021-2025.

title: Bare Soil Index
about: BSI = ((SWIR + Red) - (NIR + Blue)) / ((SWIR + Red) + (NIR + Blue)). Positive values mean exposed soil dominates even in the greenest season.
data: Sentinel-2 L2A, 10 m, Cloud Score+ masked.
used: N2 Bare soil at peak greenness.

title: Soil Erosion Risk (RUSLE)
sub: Potential soil loss A = R x K x LS x C
about: Potential soil loss from the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (support practice P = 1). Under 5 t/ha/yr is slight, 5-10 moderate, 10-20 high, over 20 very high.
data: R: CHIRPS rainfall (Singh et al. 1981); K: SoilGrids; LS: MERIT Hydro; C: Sentinel-2 NDVI.

title: Rainfall-Corrected Greenness Trend (RESTREND)
about: Each year's post-monsoon NDVI is compared with what that year's rainfall predicts, and the trend of the difference is measured. Red means decline not explained by rainfall (human-induced degradation); green means recovery.
data: Landsat 5/7/8/9 Collection 2 Level-2, 30 m; CHIRPS June-September rainfall.
used: N3 NDVI decline; degradation evidence DE3.

title: Greenness Change Since 2000-2005
about: Change in post-monsoon greenness over about 20 years; positive values mean greener today. Landsat 8/9 reads slightly higher than Landsat 5/7, so about +0.02 to +0.04 can be sensor difference.

title: Tree Cover in 2000
about: Tree canopy cover in 2000. With today's canopy, it shows whether the land was ever forested in the satellite era.
data: Hansen / UMD Global Forest Change v1.13, 30 m.

title: Year of Tree Cover Loss
about: Year in which tree cover was lost. Cells without loss are left blank.
data: Hansen / UMD Global Forest Change v1.13, 30 m.
used: Degradation evidence DE2; N6 unrecovered loss.

title: Fire Frequency 2015-2025
sub: Number of years with fire detected
about: Number of distinct years in which fire was detected. VIIRS was unavailable from January 2022 to September 2023; MODIS burned area fills the gap.
data: VIIRS 375 m active fire; MODIS MCD64A1 burned area 500 m.

title: Topographic Wetness (CTI)
about: CTI = ln(upslope area / tan slope). High values are valley floors and depressions that collect run-off; low values are ridges that shed water.

title: Vegetation and Surface Moisture (NDMI)
about: NDMI = (NIR - SWIR) / (NIR + SWIR) tracks water in leaves and the surface. Higher values mean moister vegetation and ground after the monsoon.
data: Sentinel-2 L2A, 10 m, Cloud Score+ masked.
used: Moisture context; basis of the moisture-retention layer C4.

title: Post-Monsoon Moisture Retention
about: How fast the land dries after the monsoon. Values closer to zero lose moisture slowly, so planted seedlings have water for longer.
data: Sentinel-2 L2A, 10 m, Cloud Score+ masked, 2021-2025.
used: SMC rules (driest quartile and driest half).

title: Soil Available Water Capacity
sub: Plant-available water in the top 30 cm
about: Water held between field capacity (-33 kPa) and wilting point (-1500 kPa).

title: Climatic Water Balance
sub: Mean annual rainfall minus potential evapotranspiration, 2005-2024
about: Annual water deficit: evaporative demand exceeds rainfall everywhere, so values are negative; less negative is wetter.
data: CHIRPS (~5.5 km) and MODIS MOD16A2GF PET (500 m).

title: Mean Annual Rainfall
about: Mean annual rainfall over 20 years.
used: Water balance F3; erosivity R in RUSLE; RESTREND.

title: Distance to Seasonal Water
sub: Distance to water present >= 3 months a year
about: Distance to the nearest seasonal water body, such as a tank, check-dam pond or river pool.
data: JRC Global Surface Water v1.4, 30 m.

title: Surface Water Occurrence
about: How often each 30 m cell was under water in 37 years of Landsat. 50 % or more is permanent water and is excluded (C2).
data: JRC Global Surface Water v1.4, 30 m.

title: Elevation
about: Bare-earth elevation with forests and buildings removed from the Copernicus DEM.

title: Slope
about: 5-20 % is ideal for planting with soil-moisture conservation; above 35 % is difficult; above 45 % is excluded (C4).

title: Heat Load (Aspect)
about: Combines slope, aspect and latitude: hot south-west slopes dry fastest (red), cool north-east slopes stay moister (green).

title: Slope Curvature
about: Concave ground collects water and soil; convex spurs and ridges shed them.

title: Topographic Position
sub: Elevation minus the mean of the surrounding 300 m
about: Negative values are valleys and foot-slopes with deeper soil; positive values are ridges and hill tops.

title: Height Above Nearest Drainage
sub: Vertical distance to the nearest stream
about: Low values lie close to drainage, with shallow groundwater and deeper soil.

title: Soil Depth Proxy
about: Deeper soil is expected on gentle, low-lying ground near drainage. Each part is scaled within the range here; the model uses the range + 20 km scale, so block scores can differ slightly.

title: Rockiness (Surface Roughness)
sub: Standard deviation of elevation, 7 x 7 cells
about: Rough, broken ground indicates rock outcrops and boulders.

title: Soil Clay Content
about: Clay holds water and nutrients; 18-35 % is best for most native species.

title: Soil Sand Content
about: Sandy soil drains fast and holds little water.

title: Coarse Fragments (Gravel and Stones)
about: Stony soil holds less water and is hard to dig.

title: Soil pH
about: Soil reaction; 6.0-7.5 is ideal.

title: Soil Organic Carbon
about: Organic carbon reflects soil health; it also feeds the RUSLE erodibility factor K.

title: Distance to Settlements
sub: Distance to the nearest built-up cell
about: Closer to villages means more grazing, lopping and fuelwood pressure.

title: Population Pressure
about: Relative population pressure around each cell.

title: Distance to Road
sub: Distance to the nearest mapped road
about: Road access for seedlings, water and staff (advisory only, not scored).

title: Distance to Dense Forest
about: Nearby dense forest provides seed and connectivity.
data: Meta Global Canopy Height (4.8 m level), 5 km search.

title: Protected Area
about: Area inside a notified protected area. Works need approvals consistent with its management plan.

title: Constraints (C1-C7)
sub: First constraint that applies to each cell
about: Land that cannot be planted, or must be protected. A block is excluded from the priority matrix when C2-C7 cover more than 30 % of it.
data: Meta CHM, JRC GSW, MERIT Hydro, FABDEM, WorldCover, Dynamic World, Sentinel-2.
